title: Model comparison playoffs — Apr 2025 internal memo
body:
Purpose
This memo summarizes the April 2025 model comparison "playoffs" we ran to select a default candidate for the next wave of model onboarding and to surface any regressions relative to our current production baseline. The focus was on practical signal: instruction-following helpfulness, factuality, and latency/cost tradeoffs across a composite prompt suite we use for product-facing features.

High-level conclusion (TL;DR)
- Winner for single-model default: open-variant-13B-q8 (best balance of quality and cost).
- Runner-up for high-quality tier: rw-instruct-7B-v2 (strong factuality and instruction alignment, higher per-token latency).
- Production baseline (rw-prod-3.8b) shows small regressions vs candidates on open-domain QA; keep as warm fallback for ultra-low-cost flows.
- Action: start canary onboarding of open-variant-13B-q8 in Dedicated next week, hold full rollout until canary evals and a second pass on retrieval-integration tests complete.

Evaluation setup summary
- Date range: 2025-04-01 through 2025-04-12 (experiments executed across 3 days; analysis and aggregation took the rest of the window).
- Models evaluated (final bracket): open-variant-13B-q8, rw-instruct-7B-v2, rw-prod-3.8b (baseline), gpt4o-mini-13B (partner model), tiny-eff-6B.
- Prompt suite: 820 prompts total across 6 buckets — instruction completion (220), open-domain QA (180), summarization (120), code (80), multi-step reasoning (120), persona/assistant-safety (100). Prompts drawn from internal customer logs (anonymized), docs, and synthetic edge-cases.
- Metrics collected: helpfulness (human-rated 1–5 on 900 sampled responses), factuality (binary + confidence), ROUGE-L (for summaries), exact-match (for code tasks), latency P50/P95 (ms), cost estimate ($ / 1k tokens generated).
- Statistical testing: pairwise bootstrap tests on human helpfulness at 95% CI; McNemar's tests for factuality where appropriate.

Leaderboards (aggregated score)
- Aggregated score is a weighted sum: helpfulness 45%, factuality 25%, ROUGE-L/exact-match 15%, latency penalty 15%. Lower latency and lower cost reduce the penalty. Scores normalized to 0–100.
1) open-variant-13B-q8 — 82.3 (helpfulness 4.2, factuality 0.83, ROUGE-L 0.71, P95 latency 620ms, est cost $1.8 / 1k tokens)
2) rw-instruct-7B-v2 — 79.6 (helpfulness 4.4, factuality 0.88, ROUGE-L 0.69, P95 latency 940ms, est cost $2.3 / 1k tokens)
3) gpt4o-mini-13B — 75.1 (helpfulness 4.0, factuality 0.86, ROUGE-L 0.66, P95 latency 780ms, est cost $3.1 / 1k tokens)
4) rw-prod-3.8b — 67.8 (helpfulness 3.6, factuality 0.74, ROUGE-L 0.61, P95 latency 410ms, est cost $0.9 / 1k tokens)
5) tiny-eff-6B — 60.2 (helpfulness 3.2, factuality 0.70, ROUGE-L 0.58, P95 latency 480ms, est cost $0.7 / 1k tokens)

Pairwise win/loss highlights (helpfulness, human-rated)
- open-variant-13B-q8 vs rw-instruct-7B-v2: open wins 52% of pairwise comparisons, rw-instruct wins 42%, ties 6%. Bootstrap CI indicates the gap is small but consistent (p=0.04).
- open-variant-13B-q8 vs rw-prod-3.8b: open wins 78% (p<0.001).
- rw-instruct-7B-v2 vs rw-prod-3.8b: rw-instruct wins 69% (p<0.001).

Failure modes and qualitative notes
- open-variant-13B-q8: occasional hallucinations on niche legal/medical queries (low frequency), better conversational turn-taking and persona consistency. Cost and latency are acceptable on Dedicated with q8 quantization; local debug sessions show KV cache behaves well with long-context prompts.
- rw-instruct-7B-v2: very strong at instruction rewriting and conservative answers; sometimes refuses in borderline safety cases leading to lower helpfulness on permissive prompts. Higher P95 latency observed on our CPU offload paths.
- gpt4o-mini-13B: strong multi-step reasoning but variable tokenization behavior on code tasks causing lower exact-match. Higher vendor cost but useful as a fall-through for customer-critical accuracy lanes.
- rw-prod-3.8b: fastest and cheapest; shows repeated omissions on multi-step reasoning and poor summarization on technical content.
- tiny-eff-6B: decent latency and cost; unacceptable regression on instruction-following and hallucination frequency for most customer use-cases.

Prompt-set sensitivity analysis
- We ran targeted ablations: removing persona priming, increasing context length to 2048 tokens, and swapping in more retrieval context for 120 QA prompts. Observations:
  - Persona priming improved helpfulness for chat/assistant scenarios across all models by +0.18 points on average, most for open-variant-13B-q8 (+0.27).
  - Increasing context length disproportionately increased latency for rw-instruct-7B-v2 (P95 +220ms) vs open-variant-13B-q8 (P95 +90ms), suggesting kernel/hardware mapping differences.
  - Adding retrieval snippets improved factuality for open-variant-13B-q8 from 0.83 -> 0.90 on the targeted QA subset.

Regression checks vs our production baseline
- We automatically ran the standard regression suite (1200 regression prompts including critical customer prompt-sets) comparing open-variant-13B-q8 to rw-prod-3.8b. Summary: 176 prompts flagged as potential regression candidates (open produced worse outputs) but manual triage showed 74/176 were false positives (formatting differences). Net true regressions: 102 (8.5% of suite). Root causes: hallucination on narrow domain facts (45%), tokenization truncation for long code (22%), style mismatches for terse templates (33%).

Recommendation and rollout plan
- Immediate: canary open-variant-13B-q8 to 5% traffic on Dedicated (non-critical customers) for 2 weeks. Monitor: human-helpfulness sampling, telemetry on hallucination alerts, P95 latency, and per-route cost.
- Contingency: auto-fallback to rw-prod-3.8b for latency spikes or hallucination detectors firing >X events / hour.
- Follow-up: run retrieval-integrated pass (incorporate RAG with T0 retrieval) and re-evaluate factuality on the 120 regression prompts. If net regressions fall below 2% and no critical regressions found, promote to 50% and start migration planning for Dedicated standard.
- Long-term: keep rw-instruct-7B-v2 in the high-quality tier for customers who opt into accuracy-first pricing. Test fine-tuning and safety-calibration on rw-instruct-7B-v2 if customers require conservative answers.

Open questions / risks
- Licensing and export: confirm open-variant-13B-q8 license terms for Dedicated and Private deployments (legal already pinged).
- Cost modeling: dedicated pricing above assumes 70% utilization; we need a sensitivity run for 40/90% utilization to present finance.
- Safety: persona priming improved helpfulness but may alter safety surface; coordinate with safety team for drift detection.

Appendix (short)
- Sample prompt examples used (anonymized):
  1) "Summarize the following RFC into 3 bullet points, preserving technical accuracy and any caveats."
  2) "Given this customer log, write a troubleshooting email that explains root cause and next steps."
  3) "Write a function in Python that reverses the order of words but preserves punctuation and capitalization; include tests."
  4) "If asked whether X treatment is effective for Y condition, give a short answer and cite high-level evidence or say you don't know."

- Quick sensitivity table (helpfulness delta when switching from rw-prod-3.8b to winner):
  - open-variant-13B-q8: +0.6 average helpfulness, +0.09 factuality, +0.10 ROUGE-L, latency P95 +210ms, cost +$0.9 / 1k tokens.
  - rw-instruct-7B-v2: +0.8 helpfulness, +0.14 factuality, latency P95 +530ms, cost +$1.4 / 1k tokens.

Next steps (owners)
- Canaries & telemetry hooks: Leo Zhang (infra) — due 2025-04-21
- Retrieval re-eval + regression triage: Priya Nair (applied-ml) — due 2025-04-28
- Legal license check: Legal (Ana Kaur) — due 2025-04-18
- Finance sensitivity run: Miguel Santos (finance liaison) — due 2025-04-24

Notes to reviewers
- This is intended as an operational decision memo for Product, Infra, and Legal to align on a low-risk canary. Many of the raw artifacts (full human annotations, per-prompt logs, bootstrapped CI outputs) are linked in the artifacts list above and in the PR. If you want the interactive leaderboard or raw CSVs, ping me and I will grant access.

-- Dana
